title: A base that disagrees with itself is a host fault, not an abort: recorded with the scenario and both exits, judged again after a doubling backoff, never a halt; three in a row on one mission raise an alert, recorded and delivered before objective 030 exists
prompt:
Read, in crates/spawn-cli/src/gate.rs, `Run`, `decide()` (a non-zero exit is `GateFailure::Aborted` with the gate's output: stdout, then stderr marked `! `), `NO_ROOM_EXIT` and `no_room()` (the pattern this objective follows: an exit status together with a fact the gate states); in crates/spawn-cli/src/integrate.rs the module comment (step 4, "No room is not a verdict", and the halt rules), `HALT_AFTER`, `halt_reason()`, `aborted()`, the match on `run_gate(main, &candidate)` in the judging (`Err(failure) => gated("aborted", aborted(&failure))`), `no_room()`, `room_wait()` and `room_backoff()`; in scripts/rsi/gate.sh (you may not edit it) its header (the exit-code contract: "1 (twice, from two runs that agree) = unsolved, anything else aborts the gate (exit 4, no verdict: the integrator records an abort, never a skip)"), the base results loop (`run_scenario`, `first="1, then $again"`, the line `| $objective_name exited $first on the base: a harness error, not a verdict; the gate aborts`, `stage_close aborted`, `exit 4`: the gate's only exit 4), `section`, `gate_times` (the `| gate time: base <n> s (...), candidate <n> s, setup <n> s (exports, socket scan, static checks), total <n> s` line its EXIT trap prints after the abort), scripts/stage.sh's `stage_close` (`| stage gate <result> <ms>ms <name>`) and the case "the flake is named" in scripts/rsi/test-gate.sh (it pins the line's wording on the owner's side); `spawn_integrator_record` and the `task.gated` case of `spawn_control_apply` (`gate_aborts`, `gate_rejections`, the `gate_room_*` fold) in crates/spawn-postgres/sql/schema.sql; the digest (`Why`, `Escalation::tag`) in crates/spawn-cli/src/dispatch.rs and dispatch/digest.rs, and `gate_room_escalations` in crates/spawn-cli/src/disk.rs; rsi/backlog/020.json (objective 020: the verdict `host_fault`, the mission's `gate_host_faults`, SPAWN_GATE_HOST_FAULT_BACKOFF_SECS, the escalation tagged `host gate-host-fault-<event id>`), whose vocabulary this objective extends; rsi/backlog/030.json (the alerts, and its notice `gate_base_disagrees`, which reads this objective's record); docs/fleet-architecture.md §10.3 and docs/design.md §14.

The problem. The gate judges each objective scenario on the base before any candidate code runs, and an unsolved result needs two runs that agree. When the first run exits 1 and the second 0, scripts/rsi/gate.sh prints `| 011.sh exited 1, then 0 on the base: a harness error, not a verdict; the gate aborts` and exits 4 with no verdict, and the integrator records `aborted`, which counts toward the mission's halt after three aborts in a row. On 2026-11-06 at 14:43:36 CST (06:43:36 UTC; the integrator's journal, host time +08:00) mission 4's task 87 (objective 017) was gated `aborted` that way, on 011.sh (a scenario of bounded waits: 10 s for a judgement, 30 s for a delivery), on a host so loaded that the gate's setup took 244 s instead of the usual 28; task 87 was gated again at 15:27:56 CST, accepted, and landed (58894ad on main). It is one of the four aborts the integrator's journal shows since 2026-11-04 (host time: 23:40:33, 01:58:40, 14:00:10, 14:43:36). A base whose own scenario fails and then passes says nothing about the candidate: no candidate code has run yet, and the base is code that already landed. It says the host was too loaded or too flaky to judge, which is what objective 020's `host_fault` means; yet today it is counted like a broken gate, and the next pass runs the same gate again at once on the same loaded host (0.30-0.42 s later in the scenario), so three such passes halt the mission for a person in under a second and a half. The owner's goal (2026-11-06) is the Pareto frontier: no dimension improves by letting another regress; this costs autonomy (halts) and reliability (aborts) for nothing, and changes no verdict on any work.

Owner ruling (2026-11-06). A base that disagrees with itself never counts toward a halt. Three in a row on one mission raise an alert instead of an escalation at two in a row: a `host_fault` with evidence `base_disagrees` never carries `escalate` true (020's escalation at the second in a row stays for 020's own evidence). In the owner's order this objective comes second, with 020 (028; 033 with 020; 031; 029; 030; 032), before objective 030, which owns Spawn's alerts, so (4) states how the alert is recorded until 030 exists: in the `task.gated` record itself (`alert` true, with the count), and taken to the supervisor once by the dispatcher's digest; once 030 exists its loop raises the alert `gate_base_disagrees` from that same record (030 lists it), so nothing is recorded twice and nothing is lost in between.

Required behaviour (the contract the gate checks).
1. When it applies. The gate process exits with status 4 and its stdout (as the integrator records it, before the stderr lines marked `! `) ends with the gate's own pair of lines, optionally followed by its `| gate time:` line and nothing else:
`| <name> exited 1, then 0 on the base: a harness error, not a verdict; the gate aborts`
`| stage gate aborted <ms>ms base: <name> again (unsolved needs two runs that agree)`
with the same `<name>` in both, a scenario file name (no space, no `|`). Only this pair counts: the same text with another prefix (`| | ...`, a nested gate's output inside a scenario's log, which `run_scenario` prefixes again), anywhere else in the log, or with other exits is not it. Every other gate failure stays an abort, counted, exactly as today: a first run that exits anything but 0 or 1 (`exited 2 on the base`), a second run that exits anything but 0 or 1 (`1, then 2`), a gate killed or past its wall clock, exit 3, any other status, and status 4 without the pair at its end. The integrator reads gate.sh's existing output; gate.sh does not change.
2. The verdict. Such a gate is recorded `task.gated` with verdict `host_fault` (objective 020's), not `aborted`. It is not a verdict on the work: the task stays where it was (`reported`, or `accepted` under review), its `revisions` and `review_note` do not move, nothing goes back to the worker, and neither `gate_rejections` nor `gate_aborts` moves (the rejection and abort runs neither grow nor reset). Besides `base`, `candidate`, `revision`, `scenarios` and `log` (the gate's output), the record names: `evidence` `base_disagrees`; `scenario` (`<name>`); `exits` ([1, 0], numbers); `setup_s` (the whole seconds of `setup <n> s` in the gate's `| gate time:` line, when it printed one; left out otherwise); `reason` (`host fault: the base disagrees with itself: <name> exited 1, then 0 on the base` with the setup time when known, ending `not a verdict, judged again later`); `host_faults`, `backoff_ms`, `due_ms`, `escalate` (false: see (4)), `base_disagrees` and `alert` as in (3) and (4).
3. Judged again after a backoff, never halted. As 020 requires: after the k-th host fault in a row the task waits `backoff_ms` = SPAWN_GATE_HOST_FAULT_BACKOFF_SECS (default 300) x 2^(k-1), at most one hour; `due_ms` is the record's own time (`recorded_at_ms`) plus it. Until then no pass runs a gate for the task (read from the store's record, never from memory; the mission's other tasks wait behind it as they do behind `room_wait`); once it is due the next pass judges it again. No halt rule counts a host fault, whatever its evidence.
4. One run of host faults; base disagreements alerted at three. The mission's `gate_host_faults` (020's column, in `spawn_control_apply`) is + 1 on every `host_fault`, whatever its evidence (`base_disagrees`, or 020's `failures` and `server_log`); unchanged on `no_room` and `stale`; 0 on every other verdict (`aborted` included), on `task.landed` and on `mission.resumed`: the backoff doubles across both evidences. A `host_fault` with evidence `base_disagrees` never carries `escalate` true (020's escalation at the second in a row stays for its own evidence only). Instead the mission's base disagreements in a row are counted: a new column `gate_base_disagrees`, folded in `spawn_control_apply` (+ 1 on a `host_fault` with evidence `base_disagrees`; unchanged on `no_room` and `stale`; 0 on every other verdict, 020's host faults included, on `task.landed` and on `mission.resumed`), and the record names the count, this one included, as `base_disagrees`. The one that makes it 3 carries `alert` true; every other carries `alert` false (the later ones of the same run too): three in a row raise one alert. How the alert is recorded before objective 030 exists: the `task.gated` record with `alert` true is the alert (it is named by its event id; no second record of it is written), and the dispatcher's digest takes each such record to the supervisor once, as it takes 020's escalation: an item with `session_id` `host` and id `gate-base-disagrees-<the record's event id>` (tag `host gate-base-disagrees-<id>`), whose line names the task as `task #<id>`, the mission, `<count> in a row`, the scenario, `exited 1, then 0`, the setup time when known and when the task is judged again. Once 030 exists its loop raises from the same record the alert `gate_base_disagrees` (a notice keyed by that event id), so `spawn alerts` and the dashboard show it; this objective writes no `alert.fired` record of its own, and the digest item stays. Still no halt, at three or at any count.
5. With or after 020. 020 (unsolved on the live main) introduces `host_fault`, `gate_host_faults`, the backoff and the escalation; this objective may be solved with it or after it. Solved first, it introduces them as 020 describes (020's own evidence, check-tests failures and the test server's log, stays 020's to add), and every reader of verdicts knows `host_fault`: `spawn_integrator_record` accepts it (with `evidence` `base_disagrees`, `scenario`, `exits`, `base_disagrees`, `alert`), `DELIVERY_TASKS` and the objective history treat it like `no_room` (no step change), the RSI and Missions pages show it as the host's verdict, not the work's (web/src), and the supervisor's digest names it when it lists verdicts.
6. Causality (§14): the decision rests on the gate's recorded exit status and its recorded output (the pair of lines, named in the record by `scenario` and `exits`), never on the reason's text, on time or on a scenario's name; the wait rests on the recorded `due_ms`.

How the saving shows, in numbers. Task 87's abort at 14:43:36 would have been a `host_fault`: gate_aborts unchanged, the task judged again after 300 s instead of at once on the same loaded host. Three disagreeing bases in a row, which halt a mission today (the scenario: halted 1.25-1.43 s after the first, every one a gate that judged nothing), halt nothing and reach the supervisor once, at the third, as an alert with the scenario, its exits and the gate's setup time (244 s at 14:43, against 28 s on an idle host). On 017's scorecard: reliability (aborts) and autonomy (halts a person must resume) improve; first-pass quality and rework are unchanged (no verdict on the work either way); gate time is no worse (a gate the backoff delays would have aborted again on the loaded host). None of the other objectives' scenarios may regress: 020.sh in particular keeps every check (its host faults and this one's share one run and its backoff; its escalation at the second in a row stays its own, and its host faults reset this objective's count of base disagreements).

State the rule in the module comment of integrate.rs (step 4, beside "No room is not a verdict" and 020's host fault), in `decide()`'s comment in gate.rs, and in docs/fleet-architecture.md §10.3 (the verdicts, and that no halt counts a host fault). Add unit tests in gate.rs or integrate.rs: the pair at the end of stdout with and without the gate time line, with stderr lines after it; a nested `| | ` copy of the line ignored; the pair followed by other lines ignored; `exited 2`, `1, then 2`, `1, then 3` stay `aborted`; the pair with an exit status other than 4 (0, 1, 3, 5, a signal) is not a host fault; `setup_s` read from the gate time line and left out without one; the record's fields; the backoff doubling across host faults of both 020's evidence and this one's, capped at one hour, and the hold until `due_ms`; `escalate` never for `base_disagrees`, while 020's evidence still escalates at the second in a row; `base_disagrees` counted and `alert` true only at the third in a row, reset by a real verdict, by 020's host faults, by a landing and by a resume, kept by `no_room` and `stale`; a real abort after host faults counts and resets `gate_host_faults` and `gate_base_disagrees`; no halt after any number of host faults. In crates/spawn-postgres/tests/: `spawn_integrator_record` accepts a `host_fault` with `evidence` `base_disagrees`; the fold of `gate_host_faults`, of `gate_base_disagrees` and of the task (unchanged state, revisions, gate_aborts and gate_rejections). In the dispatcher: the alert item for a record with `alert` true, its tag `host gate-base-disagrees-<id>` and its line, delivered once; no escalation item for `base_disagrees`.

The gate judges this with rsi/scenarios/033.sh (read it: its header lists today's measures). A real `spawn loop` (the Bridge, its pusher, the dispatcher, the supervisor, no model judge) runs one resident, `flaky`, of one gated mission (accept = gate) on a fake engine that writes flaky.txt and reports; `spawn integrate --once` passes, run by the scenario every half second with SPAWN_GATE_HOST_FAULT_BACKOFF_SECS=4 (and objective 018's thresholds met), judge through a recording SPAWN_GATE that prints what scripts/rsi/gate.sh prints and exits as it does: runs 1-3 a base that disagrees with itself on 011.sh (its stage lines, run 1's log holding a nested gate's `| | 102.sh exited 1, then 0 ...`, the gate's own pair, `| gate time: ... setup 244 s ...` on run 1, then 31 s and 29 s; exit 4); run 4 `| 011.sh exited 2 on the base: ...` (exit 4); run 5 `| 011.sh exited 1, then 2 on the base: ...` (exit 4); run 6 accepted. It checks:
- (1) run 1 is `host_fault`: gate_aborts and gate_rejections stay 0, the task stays `reported` with its revisions, no halt; `evidence` `base_disagrees`, `scenario` `011.sh` (not the nested gate's 102.sh), `exits` [1, 0], `setup_s` 244, `host_faults` 1 (and the mission's gate_host_faults 1), `base_disagrees` 1 (and the mission's gate_base_disagrees 1), `escalate` false, `alert` false, `backoff_ms` 4000, `due_ms` = its time + 4000;
- (2) the gate does not run again before `due_ms`, then run 2 is gated;
- (3) run 2 is `host_fault`: `host_faults` 2, `base_disagrees` 2, `backoff_ms` 8000, `due_ms`, `escalate` false, `alert` false, gate_aborts 0, no halt; no digest tagged `host gate-host-fault-<that event id>` (the escalation at two is replaced);
- (4) not before run 2's due time, run 3 is `host_fault` (`host_faults` 3, `base_disagrees` 3 and the mission's gate_base_disagrees 3, `backoff_ms` 16000, `escalate` false, `alert` true): the alert, recorded in that record; within 60 s a digest tagged `host gate-base-disagrees-<that event id>` reaches the supervisor, its line naming task #<id>, 011.sh, `1, then 0` and `3 in a row`; after two more passes the mission is not halted and gate_aborts is 0;
- (5) control, not before run 3's due time: run 4 (exit 2 first) is `aborted`, gate_aborts 1, gate_host_faults 0, gate_base_disagrees 0; run 5 (`1, then 2`) is `aborted`, gate_aborts 2; run 6 is accepted and the task lands; gate_aborts 0, the mission never halted, exactly one base-disagreement alert delivered and no host-fault escalation.
On the live main (b950e25; the deployed binary is built from it) it fails at (1): "(1) task #1, whose gate found 011.sh exiting 1 and then 0 on the base (a base that disagrees with itself, before any candidate code ran), was gated 'aborted' (the gate failed: the gate ended with exit status: 4), not 'host_fault'; gate_aborts 0 -> 1, toward the halt after three". With BB_033_MEASURE=1 (only to show today's behaviour) it goes on: no record names the scenario, its exits or the setup time (they are only in the gate's log); run 2 starts 0.34-0.42 s after run 1's record and run 3 0.30-0.34 s after run 2's, both `aborted` (gate_aborts 2, 3), with no wait; the next pass halts the mission "3 gate aborts in a row" 1.25-1.43 s after the first abort; the supervisor gets no alert; resumed by hand, runs 4 and 5 are aborted (gate_aborts 1, 2) and run 6 is accepted and lands, as (5) requires (five runs: it fails at (1) in 15-26 s; a measure run takes 31-52 s). It exits 0 when every check passes, 1 when an assertion fails, 2 on a harness failure.

Rules: never edit the protected paths, which the gate rejects: rsi/, scripts/ (scripts/rsi/, scripts/blackbox/, scripts/e2e.sh among them), deploy/, all of web/ except web/src/ and web/index.html, rust-toolchain files and .cargo/. The gate also rejects fewer runnable tests than the base (do not delete, rename, ignore or disable tests), any lint relaxation ([lints] tables, clippy.toml, a new crate-level #![allow]/#![expect], a removed #![warn]/#![deny]) and any build-time code (build.rs, .cargo/, a `build =` key in a Cargo.toml). The gate builds offline from the cargo caches already on the host: a new crate builds only if it is already in ~/.cargo/registry. Keep every existing check green (clippy -D warnings, the workspace tests, the e2e, the black-box scenarios, the web build) and add tests of your own for the new behaviour.
